Business Trip Report: Samarkand, October 12-16, 2026
Section 1. Executive Overview and Destination Details

From October 12 to October 16, 2026, a delegation of four specialists made an official five-day business trip from the central headquarters in Tashkent to Samarkand, Uzbekistan.

The main objective of the trip was to evaluate regional logistics infrastructure, audit local supply chain partners, negotiate long-term distribution agreements with regional manufacturing facilities, and oversee the preliminary setup of a new satellite operational hub in the Samarkand Free Economic Zone.

During the five working days, the team held eleven formal meetings with municipal representatives, logistics providers, and prospective corporate clients. These meetings established the foundation for the planned regional expansion in early 2027.

Business Trip Report: Samarkand, October 12-16, 2026
Section 2. Delegation Members and Assigned Roles

The delegation consisted of four team members. Each was responsible for a different operational, financial, or technical part of the trip.

Alisher Karimov, Head of Regional Operations, was the delegation lead. He led high-level negotiations with regional government officials, oversaw strategic partnerships, and signed preliminary memoranda of understanding (MoUs).

Malika Yusupova, Senior Financial Analyst, carried out on-site financial due diligence on potential local vendors, evaluated regional tax incentives, and managed the travel budget and daily expense tracking for the whole delegation.

Jasur Rakhimov, Supply Chain and Logistics Coordinator, inspected warehouse facilities, assessed transport routes connecting Samarkand to neighboring regions, and negotiated freight rates with local transport companies.

Dildora Tursunova, Legal and Compliance Specialist, reviewed regional regulatory requirements, drafted commercial contract templates, and made sure all proposed partnership agreements complied with national corporate law.

Business Trip Report: Samarkand, October 12-16, 2026
Section 3. Breakdown of Estimated Expenses

The total estimated expenditure for the five-day business trip for all four delegation members was $3,420.00 (approximately 43,776,000 UZS at a rate of 12,800 UZS per USD). Expenses were allocated across transportation, accommodation, daily subsistence, local ground transport, and business representation, in line with corporate travel policy.

Intercity transportation: round-trip Afrosiyob high-speed train tickets in Business Class between Tashkent and Samarkand for 4 delegates, at $85 per person. Total cost: $340.00.

Accommodation: 4 nights at a 4-star business hotel in central Samarkand, in 4 single standard rooms at $115 per night, including breakfast and high-speed Wi-Fi. That is $460 per person for 4 nights. Total cost: $1,840.00.

Daily per diem (meals and incidentals): the standard corporate daily allowance of $40 per person per day for 5 days, which is $200 per person. Total for 4 delegates: $800.00.

Local ground transportation: a rented corporate minivan with a dedicated driver for site visits across the industrial zone and the city center, at $50 per day for 4 days. This is a shared team expense. Total cost: $200.00.

Business representation and meetings: working dinners with key prospective partners, printed presentation materials, and meeting room rental. These costs were managed by Alisher Karimov and Malika Yusupova. Total cost: $240.00.

Total estimated expenditure for the full delegation: $3,420.00.

Business Trip Report: Samarkand, October 12-16, 2026
Section 4. Individual Expenditure Summary

Shared logistics and hotel bookings were paid centrally with the corporate travel card. Individual reimbursements and per diem payments were tracked for each employee as follows.

Alisher Karimov: $1,025.00 in total. This includes his round-trip train ticket ($85), four nights of hotel accommodation ($460), the five-day per diem ($200), a share of local transport ($50), and $230 in business representation expenses for hosting two formal partner dinners and printing executive briefing packets.

Malika Yusupova: $805.00 in total. This includes her round-trip train ticket ($85), four nights of hotel accommodation ($460), the five-day per diem ($200), a share of local transport ($50), and $10 for local courier and document notarization fees.

Jasur Rakhimov: $795.00 in total. This includes his round-trip train ticket ($85), four nights of hotel accommodation ($460), the five-day per diem ($200), and a share of local transport ($50) used during warehouse and industrial zone inspections.

Dildora Tursunova: $795.00 in total. This includes her round-trip train ticket ($85), four nights of hotel accommodation ($460), the five-day per diem ($200), and a share of local transport ($50) for legal consultations and visits to municipal registry offices.

Business Trip Report: Samarkand, October 12-16, 2026
Section 5. Key Outcomes and Financial Reconciliation

All expenses stayed within the pre-approved corporate travel ceiling of $3,600.00. The total spent was $3,420.00, which left a budget surplus of $180.00.

The original fiscal receipts, electronic train tickets, hotel folios, and signed attendance logs from partner meetings were compiled by Malika Yusupova and submitted to the central accounting department for final audit and ledger reconciliation.

The trip produced three signed letters of intent with regional suppliers. Once the Samarkand hub becomes operational, these agreements are expected to reduce regional distribution lead times by 22%.
